hypotheses.justification: This is an argument because it is instance-implicit and its variables `p` and `K` are both arguments; nothing omits it. The proof never uses it: it uses only `hx`, `hj`, `hp.out.one_le` and monoid lemmas (`pow_add`, `pow_succ`, `ring`). With `omit [CharP K p] in`, the same proof compiles. It can be deleted on its own or together with `hp`.

Its only use is `hp.out.one_le`, which gives `p - 1 + 1 = p`. The statement holds for every natural `p`. If p = 0, truncated subtraction gives p - 1 = 0, so the exponent is `j + q*0 = j` and the goal is `x^j = x^j`, closed by `simp`. If p ≥ 1, `Nat.sub_add_cancel` with `1 ≤ p` gives `p - 1 + 1 = p`, and the existing induction goes through unchanged (when p = 1 the goal is trivial again since p - 1 = 0). Proof without hp: `rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos p with rfl | hp0`, close the first case with `simp`, and run the original proof with `hp0` in place of `hp.out.one_le`. It can be deleted on its own or together with `[CharP K p]`.
